source.title: Do We Need Zero Training Loss After Achieving Zero Training Error?
source.authors: Takashi Ishida; Ikko Yamane; Tomoya Sakai; Gang Niu; Masashi Sugiyama

record.tranche_reason: Measures training accuracy while flooding deliberately prevents training loss from approaching zero, bearing on whether zero training error can persist without zero training loss.
record.gate_note: The benchmark comparison reports test accuracy, which does not itself measure the claim. Figure 3 measures training accuracy against flood level; the text says the validation-selected flood level is often at zero error. Other cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 3 directly measures training classification accuracy, including ResNet-44 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, under a modified training objective. Flooding prevents zero surrogate loss; it does not deliberately induce zero classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: validation-selected flooding often retains zero training error while preventing zero training loss, and flooding improves test performance in various experiments. The authors also establish a conditional risk-estimator MSE result.
record.recipe_differences: Flooding modifies the objective to reverse the gradient below a chosen positive loss level; benchmark training uses SGD, while synthetic experiments use Adam. The study does not reproduce the unmodified training recipe as its central intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy declines as the flood level increases; the plotted results also distinguish early stopping from no early stopping.

fits_no_version.finding: Flooding often improves test accuracy while maintaining positive training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preventing further surrogate-loss minimization can improve generalization without necessarily sacrificing training classification accuracy.

record.problems: The claim-relevant training-accuracy results are presented in Figure 3 without numerical values in the text. The authors describe selected flood levels as often, rather than always, corresponding to zero error.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 and Table 3 report test accuracy, not training error. Figures 2, 4, and 5 report test loss, gradients, or loss landscape and do not independently measure the version's training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random labels on CIFAR; model-size dependence; small-model failures; Adam on CIFAR; and an explicit comparison of initialization choices. Label-noise experiments use synthetic data and MLPs, and their reported outcomes are test accuracy.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and matched shortcut comparisons.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories and recovery or divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance; normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Separate CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 ResNet-44 training-accuracy results at b=0, validation-selected flood levels and higher flood levels, distinguishing augmentation/learning-rate decay and early stopping. These are needed to identify zero-error support and any meaningful departure from near-zero training error.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Figure 3(a–b); experimental conditions in Section 4.2

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is justified by the recoverable aggregate description: the zero-error selected settings are unidentified, and decreasing accuracy alone does not establish substantial training error in the CIFAR conditions. Higher flooding is an intentional regularization intervention, so its effects would qualify that recipe rather than challenge ordinary SGD's ability to fit the data.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test random or corrupted labels, compare network widths, or establish the claim across SGD and Adam. Its benchmark experiments use original labels; the relevant training-error result is reported for flooding levels, not a systematic comparison of small and large models.

rows.subject: All datasets and settings (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train with flooding over a sweep of flood levels; measure training accuracy of the trained model.
rows.measure: Training accuracy of trained model versus flood level; authors state the curves decrease as flood level rises and validation-selected flood levels are often at zero error.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the plotted datasets and settings; no per-model values are recoverable from the text.
rows.check: The aggregate combines CIFAR convolutional networks relevant to V1 with MNIST/KMNIST MLPs and SVHN outside its stated setting. It also combines flood levels with different outcomes. Split by dataset, recipe and flood level. The text reports decreasing training accuracy and some zero-error selected settings, but does not identify which CIFAR settings achieve zero error. A single partial state is unsupported.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Validation-selected flood levels across the reported datasets and settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that selected flood levels are often plotted at zero error, consistent with retaining zero training error while training loss is kept positive (R1, R2).
